You'll own the user interfaces our customers touch every day. That means features in the React panel, pages on the Astro website, and the PHP and HTML templates behind our billing and other systems. This isn't a junior role. You should be able to take a feature from an issue to a reviewed pull request with little hand-holding. You should also be able to read code you didn't write and know when to ask a question. Backend experience is a real plus but not required. If you're strong on the frontend and want to grow into full-stack work, we'll train you on our PHP/Laravel backend and the systems around it. **What you'll work on** Most of your time goes to the first two areas. The rest grows as you do. * **Pine Game Panel** (React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, styled-components, easy-peasy, React Router; Laravel API): build and polish customer features such as the file manager, console, backups, schedules, mod and plugin installers, template shop and game-specific settings screens * **Website** (Astro, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4): product and game pages, pricing, tools and blog; keep it fast, accessible and SEO-friendly * **Billing and client area** (WHMCS: PHP, Smarty templates, HTML/CSS/JS): customize the client area, order flow and email templates; write hooks * **Internal tools** (React + Vite; ASP.NET Core): admin dashboards for staff, such as product data, sponsorships and hardware planning * **Panel backend, as you grow** (PHP 8.2+, Laravel 12, MySQL, Redis, queues): API endpoints, services, background jobs, tests On the panel, there is also modernization work ahead. Planned items include moving off twin.macro to plain Tailwind, upgrading React and Tailwind, and reworking layouts to be truly responsive. If you enjoy leaving a codebase better than you found it, there's plenty to do. **What we're looking for** * Around 2–4 years of professional or equivalent real-world frontend experience, with shipped work you can show us * Strong React and TypeScript: hooks, component design, state management, and talking to REST APIs * Solid HTML and CSS fundamentals, with Tailwind CSS experience; responsive layouts, accessibility and cross-browser quirks shouldn't scare you * Comfort with plain PHP and server-rendered HTML templates, sin
